cleaned_text: HDFC ELSS Tax Saver Fund - Official Scheme Page HDFC ELSS Tax Saver Fund AMC: HDFC Asset Management Company Limited Category: ELSS (Equity Linked Savings Scheme) - An open-ended equity linked saving scheme with a statutory lock-in of 3 years and tax benefit under Section 80C. Fund Type: Open-Ended ELSS (Tax Saving) Scheme Launch Date: March 31, 1996 Plan Options: Direct Plan and Regular Plan, available in Growth and IDCW (Income Distribution cum Capital Withdrawal) options. Also known as: HDFC Tax Saver Fund, HDFC ELSS Fund Direct Growth, HDFC Tax Saving Fund Net Asset Value (NAV) & Assets Under Management (AUM) Net Asset Value (NAV): As of June 01, 2026, the Net Asset Value (NAV) for HDFC ELSS Tax Saver Fund is Rs. 1,250.60 for the Direct Plan and Rs. 1,080.25 for the Regular Plan. Assets Under Management (AUM): As of April 30, 2026, the Assets Under Management (AUM) for HDFC ELSS Tax Saver Fund is Rs. 15,890 Crores. NAV History: The NAV of the Direct Plan was Rs. 1,045.30 on June 01, 2025, Rs. 780.60 on June 01, 2023, and Rs. 420.15 on June 01, 2019. Fund Manager The fund is managed by Mr. Roshi Jain and co-managed by Mr. Dhruv Muchhal . Mr. Jain has been managing this fund since 2022 and brings a value-oriented investment philosophy. The fund management team focuses on identifying fundamentally strong companies across market capitalizations that offer long-term wealth creation potential while keeping the 3-year lock-in period in mind for position sizing. Lock-in Period & Tax Benefits HDFC ELSS Tax Saver Fund has a mandatory lock-in period of 3 years from the date of allotment of each unit. This is the shortest lock-in among all tax-saving investment options under Section 80C of the Income Tax Act, 1961. Tax Deduction under Section 80C: Investments up to Rs. 1,50,000 per financial year in HDFC ELSS Tax Saver Fund qualify for deduction under Section 80C. This reduces the investor's taxable income, leading to tax savings of up to Rs. 46,800 (at the highest tax bracket of 30% + 4% cess). Comparison with other 80C options: ELSS has the shortest lock-in (3 years) compared to PPF (15 years), NSC (5 years), Tax Saving FD (5 years), and NPS (till retirement). ELSS also offers the potential for higher returns through equity market exposure. Scheme Suitability & Riskometer This product is suitable for investors who are seeking long-term capital appreciation along with tax benefits under Section 80C. The riskometer for HDFC ELSS Tax Saver Fund is classified as Very High . Suitable for investors with moderate to high risk appetite and ability to stay invested for at least 3 years (mandatory lock-in). Benchmark The benchmark index for HDFC ELSS Tax Saver Fund is the Nifty 500 TRI (Total Returns Index). Historical Returns & Performance The following are the historical returns for HDFC ELSS Tax Saver Fund (Direct Plan) as of May 31, 2026: 1-Year Return: 18.20% (Benchmark: 17.50%) 3-Year Return (CAGR): 19.75% (Benchmark: 19.30%) 5-Year Return (CAGR): 21.30% (Benchmark: 18.20%) 10-Year Return (CAGR): 16.85% (Benchmark: 15.10%) Since Inception Return (CAGR): 20.50% (Benchmark: 15.80%) Note: Past performance may or may not be sustained in the future. Tax-Adjusted Returns: Considering the Section 80C tax benefit, the effective returns for an investor in the 30% tax bracket are significantly higher. For a Rs. 1,50,000 investment, the immediate tax saving of Rs. 46,800 effectively reduces the initial outlay. Portfolio Composition & Sector Allocation As of April 30, 2026, the portfolio of HDFC ELSS Tax Saver Fund holds approximately 50 stocks. Market cap allocation: Large Cap 60%, Mid Cap 28%, Small Cap 12%. The key sector allocation is: Financial Services & Banking: 29.5% Information Technology: 14.2% Healthcare & Pharmaceuticals: 10.5% Consumer Discretionary: 9.8% Automobile & Auto Ancillaries: 8.2% Oil, Gas & Energy: 7.5% Industrials: 6.8% Others: 13.5% Top 5 holdings: ICICI Bank Ltd (8.5%), HDFC Bank Ltd (7.5%), Infosys Ltd (5.8%), Bharti Airtel Ltd (4.8%), and Axis Bank Ltd (4.2%). Investment Details & Minimum Amounts Minimum SIP Amount: Rs. 500 per month and in multiples of Rs. 500 thereafter. Minimum Initial Investment (Lumpsum): Rs. 500 and in multiples of Rs. 500 thereafter. Minimum Additional Purchase: Rs. 500 and in multiples of Rs. 500 thereafter. Maximum Investment for 80C benefit: Rs. 1,50,000 per financial year (combined limit under Section 80C). SIP Frequency Options: Monthly and Quarterly SIP options are available. Important: Each SIP installment is treated as a fresh investment and has its own 3-year lock-in period. Expense Ratio As of April 30, 2026, the Expense Ratio for HDFC ELSS Tax Saver Fund is: Direct Plan: 0.98% per annum Regular Plan: 1.85% per annum Exit Load Details The exit load for HDFC ELSS Tax Saver Fund is Nil . Since the scheme has a mandatory 3-year lock-in period, no exit load is applicable upon redemption after the lock-in period. Units cannot be redeemed before the completion of the 3-year lock-in period from the date of allotment of each unit. Tax Implications Section 80C Deduction: Investment up to Rs. 1,50,000 per financial year is eligible for deduction from taxable income under Section 80C. Lock-in: Mandatory 3-year lock-in from allotment date of each unit. Short-Term Capital Gains (STCG): Not applicable as units cannot be sold within 12 months due to the 3-year lock-in. Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG): Gains exceeding Rs. 1.25 lakh per financial year are taxed at 12.5% (plus applicable surcharge and cess) upon redemption after the lock-in period. Dividend (IDCW): Taxable at investor's slab rate. TDS of 10% for dividends exceeding Rs. 5,000. SIP Calculator & Wealth Creation A monthly SIP of Rs. 10,000 in the Direct Plan of HDFC ELSS Tax Saver Fund, started 10 years ago, would have grown to approximately Rs. 28.8 Lakhs (total investment of Rs. 12 Lakhs), with additional tax savings of up to Rs. 4,68,000 over 10 years (assuming 30% tax bracket). A monthly SIP of Rs. 12,500 optimally utilizes the full Rs. 1,50,000 annual 80C limit. Risk Factors Lock-in Risk: Units cannot be redeemed for 3 years, even in case of market downturns or personal liquidity needs. Market Risk: Being an equity fund, NAV is subject to market volatility. Concentration Risk: Large allocation to financial services sector. Tax Policy Risk: Future changes in Section 80C limits or ELSS tax treatment may impact the tax benefit proposition. How to Invest Investors can invest through: HDFC MF website, mobile app, Groww, Zerodha, Kuvera, Paytm Money, authorized distributors, and bank branches. For tax planning, investors should ensure investments are made before March 31st of the financial year. Last updated from sources: June 01, 2026.
